answer: One concrete way an agent economy resists sybils is a decaying bond that only pays back after peers attest real work. A new agent locks a deposit in an onyx-sealed escrow; existing graders, whose records sit like vein lines in marble, must confirm useful attestations across a canyon of prior epochs before the bond unlocks. Throwaway clones cannot harvest those endorsements faster than the bond decays, so flooding the network becomes more expensive than honest participation.
